newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt panel mulls streamlining of ministries.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt panel mulls streamlining of ministries.

text.p: A panel chaired by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto is considering streamlining government ministries, but stopped short of coming up with concrete steps in its mid-term report released on Thursday.

Among the issues discussed by panel members were the possibility of setting up government agencies to take over some of the workload of ministries and measures to strengthen the power of the cabinet, the report said.
Some members proposed making the agencies responsible for implementing policies and limiting the role of the ministries to policy planning.
On the role of the cabinet, some members said the leadership of the prime minister should be strengthened.
The prime minister should take the lead in broader areas of policy, including the formation of the budget, the report cited some members as saying.
Currently, the government's draft budget requires cabinet approval, but the process of forming the budget is almost completely in the hands of the Finance Ministry.
The panel will put together a final report by the end of November and aims to implement its reform measures from the start of the year 2001 at the latest.
